scenarios: missing trusted context cannot be replaced by event identity
a mismatched AppID is rejected
server allowlist must be configured
platform userInfo metadata is ignored instead of trusted
create derives owner and timestamps on the server
root owner injection is rejected
owner and metadata injection inside editable fields is rejected
object-shaped query operators cannot masquerade as a title
blank, oversized, enum, boolean and calendar inputs fail
valid leap day and empty date are accepted
list returns only current owner records
cross-owner get and missing get have the same public outcome
cross-owner update is rejected without changing a record
cross-owner delete is rejected without deleting a record
owned update increments version and preserves owner and creation time
stale versions cannot overwrite a newer update
two concurrent submissions with one version have one winner
delete checks version before removing
updating deleted records never recreates them
invalid IDs and versions are stopped before database writes
list input limits and filters are validated
keyset pagination is complete without leaking another owner
done and pending filters still enforce ownership
database operations all contain ownerAppId and ownerId predicates
unexpected database failures do not expose internal error messages
unsupported operations and non-object requests fail explicitly
real cloud entry is wired to SDK context rather than input
client does not call cloud before configuration
client distinguishes transport failure from business rejection
client rejects malformed cloud envelopes
successful editor submission is not repeated
uncertain write results retain draft and block blind resubmission
a rejected stale edit preserves the draft without claiming saved
an unloaded editor ignores late success but cannot undo the write
database template denies direct client reads and writes
SDK is pinned and the project keeps the cloud function directory separate
limitations: In-memory database and SDK stubs only. Actual cloud deployment, SDK/database execution, security-rule enforcement, and two-account tests remain manual.
